title: The connection between institutions and economic development — the work of the 2024 Nobel laureates in economics
title_hu: Az intézmények és a gazdasági fejlődés kapcsolata — a 2024-es közgazdasági Nobel-díjasok munkássága
summary_en: The 2024 economics Nobel went to Acemoglu, Johnson and Robinson for their work on institutions and economic development. Kónya reviews their research programme in this Hungarian Financial and Economic Review article — from the original colonial-origins paper on the role of property rights, through state-formation comparative work, to the recent technology-and-political-economy synthesis — and discusses what it implies for thinking about Hungarian institutional reform and the institutional roots of CEE growth divergence.
policy_relevance: Useful policy-context input for Hungarian institutional and competitiveness debates (MNB Competitiveness Report, NGM medium-term planning, ITM industrial-strategy framing). The 2024 Nobel-laureates' framework is a rigorous lens for analysing Hungary's relative growth trajectory within CEE — and for assessing the long-run consequences of contested institutional reforms (judicial independence, anti-corruption institutions, capacity of the regulatory state).
